items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including security feature bypass, arbitrary code execution, and privilege escalation. It also addresses an unauthenticated customer account takeover with a CVSS score of 9.1.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization leading to Privilege Escalation
items.summary: An Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce could result in privilege escalation, allowing an attacker to gain elevated access to sensitive resources without user interaction.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization leading to Security Feature Bypass
items.summary: An Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce could allow a low-privileged attacker to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized read and write access, causing limited disruption to availability.

items.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
items.summary: Adobe Commerce is affected by a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability that a low-privileged attacker could abuse to inject malicious scripts into vulnerable form fields.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities that could lead to arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, and security feature bypass.

items.title: Critical Remote Code Execution vulnerabilities in Amasty extensions
items.summary: Amasty issued a massive security release for dozens of extensions, with two critical vulnerabilities that can lead to remote code execution.

items.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload in Amasty Order Attributes for Magento
items.summary: An unauthenticated arbitrary file upload flaw in Amasty Order Attributes allows attackers to write executable files to a Magento store without logging in, opening the door to remote code execution.

items.title: PolyShell: unrestricted file upload in Magento and Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Sansec discovered a critical flaw in Magento's REST API that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload executable files to any store, with a fix released in Magento 2.4.9 on May 12, 2026.
